claims.text: ``explicit`` is deliberately not touched here. structcore has no branch context, so its edge set contains the dead-branch and swallowed-import edges ``_split_imports`` withheld two blocks up; merging them back turned every one of those refusals into a silent ``reachable``.
claims.why: The claim refers to structcore, _split_imports, and merging behavior that are not present in this chunk. The code does not modify explicit, but the reasoning about structcore and _split_imports cannot be verified.

claims.text: Sharing them stopped a tier's walk dead at any module some other entry had already claimed -- ``spine/picker.py`` carries a __main__ guard, so it was claimed at depth 0 and the ``cli:improve`` walk never got through it to attempt.py or worktree.py, which then degraded to the coarsest attribution available. Traversal must cross claimed nodes; only the first tier to ARRIVE writes the claim.
claims.why: The claim references specific modules (spine/picker.py, cli:improve, attempt.py, worktree.py) and a previous bug that are not present in this chunk. The comment explains the design, but the actual behavior of the BFS with per-tier visited sets cannot be fully verified without seeing the rest of the code and the specific modules.
